description.value: The study investigated gender differences in emotional reactivity and cognitive reappraisal-related emotion regulation using fMRI.

spans.text: The present study addresses critical gaps in the literature by investigating gender differences in emotional reactivity and regulation.

value: We hypothesized that men and women would show comparable reactivity, as indexed by increases in self-reported emotional experience and activity in emotion-related regions such as the amygdala.
We hypothesized that gender differences would emerge when considering the comparison between unregulated responding and cognitive regulation.
we predicted that women would show lesser decreases in negative affect due to regulation
We also predicted that these smaller decreases in emotional responding in women would be accompanied by lesser increases in prefrontal regions known to be involved in cognitive control.

description.value: Twenty-five participants were recruited; 13 were women and 12 were men. Participants completed an event-related within-subject emotion regulation task during fMRI.

spans.text: We used an established within-subjects functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) paradigm to create conditions of unregulated responding and cognitive regulation using validated negative stimuli.
